data.description: Applying specified protective coatings to Melbourne commercial and industrial surfaces. Hardstand, plant rooms, bunded areas and walkways, with substrate preparation and documentation to the specification.

mainEntity.name: Can you work to our engineer's specification?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, and that is the normal arrangement on this kind of work. Send the specification at quote stage. If anything in it looks wrong for the substrate we will raise it in writing rather than substituting a product quietly.

mainEntity.name: How do you test whether the slab is dry enough?

acceptedAnswer.text:
With the method the specification calls for, which is usually a relative humidity probe or a calcium chloride test depending on the system. A plastic sheet taped down overnight is an indicator rather than a test.

Moisture is the single most common cause of coating failure on commercial concrete and it is entirely avoidable.

mainEntity.name: What if there is already a coating on it?

acceptedAnswer.text:
It gets identified before anything else, because compatibility decides the whole job. An unknown coating is tested, and where the new system cannot bond to it the slab has to be stripped or ground back.

A fresh coat over an incompatible or failing one delaminates, usually within months.

mainEntity.name: Do you provide documentation of what was applied?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes: products, batch details where relevant, preparation method, substrate test results and coverage rates. On commercial work that record is often more useful to the client than the coating itself, because it is what a warranty claim or an audit rests on.

mainEntity.name: Can you coat a bunded area?

acceptedAnswer.text:
We can apply a specified system to one. What we will not do is tell you which system a bund legally requires, because that depends on what is being contained and it is an engineering and compliance question.

Get the specification, and we will apply it properly and document it.
